title: Represent capabilities and automation recipes as typed Board objects
summary: Extend BoardCore with versioned capability, trigger, condition, action, policy and receipt nodes so cross-app automations can be visually composed without reducing them to untyped boxes and arrows.
acceptance_criteria: The repository publishes a versioned capability descriptor with a repository-qualified capability ID, owning repository/revision, schema version, purpose, maturity and deprecation state.
Inputs, outputs and errors reference typed artifact or domain schemas with explicit sensitivity, retention, freshness and provenance rather than opaque dictionaries.

The first published descriptor covers these repository-owned capabilities: place capability nodes; connect typed recipe edges; inspect compatibility and permissions; export a validated automation proposal.
Preconditions, postconditions, invariants, forbidden states and documented side effects are separated and machine-readable.
The descriptor declares required read, write, execute, network, credential, hardware, external communication and destructive permissions individually; capability availability never grants them.
Synchronous, asynchronous, streaming and long-running behavior is explicit together with timeout, cancellation, retry, deduplication, ordering and idempotence semantics.
A deterministic dry-run or scenario adapter exercises the capability without live mutation and labels synthetic, fixture, simulator, device, hardware and production evidence honestly.
Compatibility ranges cover capability version, payload schemas, platform/runtime requirements, required peer capabilities and known incompatible combinations.
Unknown versions, stale descriptors, revoked capabilities, missing dependencies, partial availability and unsupported environments have explicit refusal or fallback behavior.
A capability result emits a typed receipt and quality evidence with stable observation IDs, limitations and correlation to the originating Work Package or handoff.
User-facing name, purpose, risk summary and confirmation copy are localized and accessible; machine identifiers never become the only explanation.
Descriptor generation is derived from repository-owned source or validated fixtures and does not create a second manually maintained source of truth.
No raw application database, credentials or unrelated private payload is copied into HumbleControl, the registry or another application.
Contract updates invalidate or supersede affected registry and digital-twin projections instead of silently changing the meaning of an existing version.
Canonical fixtures cover success, missing permission, stale input, duplicate request, timeout, cancellation, unsupported version, partial result and revoked capability.
Producer conformance, repository-native tests, documentation, artifact checks and the strongest practical zero-warning gate pass.

agent_notes: Portfolio Composability & Automation Wave 7; repository-owned capability and safe automation planning ticket.
Estimated effort: L to XL after all prerequisites; split implementation into bounded Work Packages.
Implementation risk: medium-high; safety class: visual-authoring.
Non-scope: Do not execute the visual flow, grant permissions, hide incompatible edges or mutate app source truth from the composer.

Alternative considered and rejected: Draw automations as generic diagram nodes — rejected because generic nodes cannot prove schema compatibility, permission requirements, error routing or executable identity.
Run a fresh delta review against the current default branch before publication or implementation.

Wave 8 portfolio reassessment: retain-conditional; priority band later. Capability and automation contracts may support the professional environment, but each application remains independent by default.
Wave 10 final rationalization: consolidate-into-agent-platform; portfolio band later. Keep capability and automation contracts as bounded platform work, not app-wide requirements.
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `optional-reference-or-research`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-research`, relevance `later`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `bounded platform pilot with explicit permissions`. Capability and automation contracts may support the platform environment but remain optional until concrete operators exist.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-platform-research` / `later` / priority `medium`. Generic capability and automation layers remain optional until dogfooding proves value.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid-research-or-reference`; publication `publish-as-proposed-backlog`; implementation sequence `later`. Generic capability and automation layers remain optional until dogfooding proves value.
